newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia changes Wednesday T-bill auction.
newsitem.headline: Russia changes Wednesday T-bill auction.

text.p: The Russian finance ministry will auction two new 4.00 trillion rouble tranches of existing GKO discount Treasury bills, running for 203 and 231 days respectively, on Wednesday, instead of the planned 7.00 trillion rouble auction of new 273-day paper, the central bank said on Tuesday.
Finance Ministry officials said the change was being made because of uncertainty about a new tax on earnings from government securities.
The new tax, which technically came into force last week, applies only to new issues, not issues already in circulation or new tranches of such older issues.
The authorities made a similar substitution last week.
Details of the new tranches to be auctioned:
The two new tranches replace a planned new issue with the following terms:
The series 22065 bills closed on Tuesday at 84.83, yielding 32.00 percent, and the series 22060 bills closed at 83.04, yielding 32.13 percent.
Plans to issue on Wednesday a new 4.00 trillion rouble 504-day tranche of the 18-month OFZ interest-bearing government bond maturing in June 1998 remain unchanged.
The new tax imposes the usual profits tax, which is 43 percent for banks and 35 percent for other entities, on government securities, while setting a 15 percent rate on interest from bond coupons.
Government officials had intended the new tax to be levied at a rate of 15 percent on all earnings from government securities, including gains on discount paper.
The Finance Ministry and Federal Tax Service have written to the Justice Ministry saying the tax should be interpreted in this way, but the Justice Ministry has not yet approved this letter.
